newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Chirac says econ ties to reinforce political ones.
newsitem.headline: Chirac says econ ties to reinforce political ones.

text.p: French President Jacques Chirac said on Thursday political ties with future European Union partners must be reinforced with strong economic links and called for more French investment in the Czech Republic.

Speaking to a forum of French and Czech businessmen on the second day of a state visit to the Czech Republic, Chirac said France had recently slipped to fifth from third place on the list of countries investing in the Czech Republic.

"We have to redress this situation," he said adding that the decline in France's position among investors was due to the absence of any French investment in the privatisation of the Czech telecommunications sector.
France has only a three to four percent share of the Czech market, dwarfed by Germany's 30 percent.
Chirac also re-iterated his "unreserved support" for Czech membership of the EU by the year 2000.
The Czechs, along with Poland and Hungary, are the leading candidates to become the next new members of both the EU and North Atlantic Treaty Organisation (NATO).
"You know the importance that I attach to our political relations with our future European Union partners being re-inforced by strong, balanced bilateral economic ties," Chirac told the forum.

Chirac called on French businessmen to be more daring and persistant in their efforts in the Czech Republic, highlighting nuclear safety as an area where firms could be successful as the Czechs finish construction of the Temelin nuclear power plant.

The often-delayed Temelin plant is expected to be completed by April 1999. "Why should we not engage in true cooperation, in particular to train operators and security personnel (at Temelin)," he said.
Chirac was due to meet Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus later in the day, and then address the Czech parliament prior to his departure.
